variables.claim_asserts: Each successive increment leaves the enlarged spirally grown structure geometrically similar to its pre-existing form.
variables.test_measures: Ontogenetic log-ranges of conch width index CWI, umbilical width index UWI, and whorl expansion rate WER, classifying a series as allometric when any index changes by at least 50%.

modality.note: Repeated shape-index measurements along individual ammonoid conchs are the appropriate geometric modality for testing whether increments are gnomons.

assumptions.note: The dm >= 2 mm cutoff excludes embryonic ammonitella not formed by the terminal accretion at issue; the 25% and 50% tolerances are declared conventions rather than author-specified boundaries.

scope.claim_scope: Molluscan shells and opercula, foraminiferal chambers, horns, and tusks showing logarithmic-spiral growth.
scope.test_scope: 179 post-embryonic ontogenetic series from 177 Devonian-Jurassic ammonoid species.

reasons: CWI, UWI, and WER are dimensionless descriptors of conch similarity, so their constancy is the geometric condition that a new increment be a gnomon.
The pre-registered refutation requires at least two thirds allometric; 168 of 179 series qualify because at least one index changes by 50% or more.
The result is driven by UWI, with median change 204.2% and 91.6% of series exceeding 50%, while WER is mostly stable; this still measures whole-conch similarity asserted by the claim.
The interpretation explicitly limits the evidence to ammonoid conchs and notes that gastropods, opercula, foraminifera, horns, and tusks were not tested.
what_would_change_it: Measure successive dimensionless shape indices in gastropods, opercula, foraminiferal chambers, horns, and tusks, or narrow the claim-level conclusion explicitly to ammonoid conchs.
